lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: Quiet is the right word for a club still being remade, and Toronto has earned that calm with a summer of nibbling around the edges rather than tearing at the seams. The most telling move came Friday, when the Maple Leafs signed Brendan Brisson to a one-year contract - a low-risk swing on a former first-round pick who can push for a depth role when camp opens later this month. That's the story now: not fireworks, but fit. Auston Matthews still sets the tone, and Jack Roslovic is the cleanest bet to add speed and a right-shot jolt to the middle six. Toronto has work left, but the board is clearer than it was a week ago. Training camp will tell whether Brisson is insurance or inventory, and whether Roslovic can become more than a useful piece.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Blue Jays have finally stopped looking like a team stuck between identities - and that matters more than any old winter shopping list. Jameson Taillon left his return start with right elbow discomfort, a sour turn for a club trying to hold its new shape together after the deadline shakeup. Toronto sits at 70-71, and that record tells the story plainly: not dead, not dangerous, just stubbornly alive. Alejandro Kirk, Ernie Clement and George Springer drove in two runs apiece in the 9-2 win over Kansas City, and the noise around the club is all about belief, not panic. Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s resurgence keeps the lineup from feeling ordinary, while the Taillon scare reminds everyone how thin the pitching margin remains. Watch the MRI, then watch how Ross Atkins handles the winter's pitching market.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The quiet ended the moment Kawhi Leonard's return to Toronto stopped being rumor and started looking inevitable - and that is the entire offseason in one hard, glittering snapshot. The Raptors are being handed a star who can change the room, the pecking order and the temperature of the whole East; after a season that finished at 0-0 in the standings' sense of current relevance, the only thing that matters now is fit. Scottie Barnes remains the spine, but Leonard is the story, the blade and the warning label. The headlines about whether Toronto should revisit the price are real because this move is expensive in picks, money and patience. Watch the paperwork, the physical, and how the depth chart shakes out once camp opens.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The summer's verdict has already landed in Washington - and it isn't flattering. Six executives ranked the Commanders near the bottom of the NFC, a blunt reminder that the shine around this roster has worn thin, even after a busy offseason overhaul. The record is old news now; what matters is the work ahead, because a team that finished 5-12 cannot survive on reputation alone. Sonny Styles is the name to watch, the rookie linebacker carrying the promise of speed, range and a cleaner defensive identity. Zach Ertz's reunion talk adds a bittersweet wrinkle, but the real story is whether this front can turn all that personnel churn into something sturdier than paper depth. What to watch next: camp battles, health up front and whether Daniels gets a supporting cast worthy of the hype.

article.title: Saturday's Skate
paragraphs: Auston Matthews set the tone in Leafs camp talk, and Jack Roslovic is already a name to watch as the Maple Leafs shape their 2026-27 forward group. The Blue Jays found a timely lift against the Royals, and the conversation around Toronto keeps circling whether that bat can travel into the next stretch.
